Script lines run on an Ollama worker node before it starts pulling tasks

ollama_worker_script_lines.Rd

Loads the module chain Spartan's GPU partition requires for Ollama (GCCcore -> ollama -> foss/R, matching the example scripts on the server), points OLLAMA_MODELS at the model store directory, sets OLLAMA_NOPRUNE=1 to prevent the server from pruning unused models (the dispatcher pulls once; workers must only check for existence), starts the cluster's run_ollama_server wrapper (Spartan's own wrapper around ollama serve — not called directly) in the background, waits for it to respond, then checks that the model exists in the store. Workers never pull; only the dispatcher does (ADR 0007).

Usage

ollama_worker_script_lines(
  model,
  gres_gpu = "gpu:1",
  model_store = model_store_dir()
)

Arguments

model

Ollama model identifier

gres_gpu

Value for the --gres SLURM directive, e.g. "gpu:1" (default) or "gpu:2" for a model that needs more than one GPU's VRAM

model_store

Path to the model store directory (default: model_store_dir())

Value

A character vector of shell script lines

Details

Unlike a plain ollama serve, Spartan's run_ollama_server binds to a random port each time (it shares GPU nodes across users, so port 11434 can't be assumed free) and only reports the chosen host:port in its own stdout, e.g. OLLAMA_HOST=spartan-gpgpu126:34267 ollama <CMD>. So this redirects that stdout to a log file, polls it until the OLLAMA_HOST=... line appears, and exports it — plus OLLAMA_BASE_URL (the env var ellmer::chat_ollama() actually reads, in http://host:port form) — before probing readiness, so every later command in the job (the readiness curl, the model check, and the R worker process itself) talks to the right port instead of silently falling back to the unused default of 11434.

The server log is written to ollama-logs/<sanitised model>_$SLURM_JOB_ID.log rather than a fixed relative name: every GPU worker job runs from the same checkout-root working directory (one crew.cluster SLURM job per model, ADR 0001), so a shared plain filename like ollama-server.log is clobbered by every concurrent model's worker (and by crew's own relaunch of a timed-out worker for the same model) — a worker can read another worker's OLLAMA_HOST= line, or a truncated/interleaved one. Keying the path on both the model slug and $SLURM_JOB_ID (always set inside an sbatch job) gives every worker job its own file.

This log also contains the TTY progress-bar redraw sequences run_ollama_server/ollama pull emit, which makes grep treat the file as binary and, without -a, print "binary file matches" instead of the actual match — silently breaking the OLLAMA_HOST extraction. Both grep calls here force text mode with -a to avoid that, and the result is checked for emptiness (failing the job immediately with a clear message) rather than letting a blank OLLAMA_HOST silently produce a hostless OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http:// that only surfaces later as a confusing ellmer/httr2 URL-parsing error.

The leading #SBATCH --gres=gpu:<n> line requests the GPU(s). gres_gpu lets this be e.g. "gpu:2" for a model too large for one A100's VRAM — see gres_gpu in slurm-resources.yml (ADR 0001). crew.cluster::crew_controller_slurm() has no dedicated gres argument, but sbatch keeps scanning for #SBATCH directives up to the first non-comment line, and crew.cluster places script_lines immediately after its own generated header with no other commands in between — so a #SBATCH line is still honoured here as long as it comes first.
